paper_title: Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models
caption: Random (light color) and random (darker color) performance comparison with different perturbation setups and the unperturbed trained model variants (orange bars). Left-to-right: Blue: Accuracy of the embedding and first layers' probes; Green: Random models with pre-trained embedding layer: no perturbation, , , , ; Red: Random models where the embedding layer is random as well: no perturbation, , , , ; Orange: Unperturbed trained models.
model_annotation: This bar chart compares the accuracy of various model variants, including perturbed and unperturbed versions. The horizontal axis contains categories of model variants, and the vertical axis represents accuracy, labeled as "Accuracy", with a scale ranging from 70 to 95. The categories on the horizontal axis are labeled as follows: embedding, 1st layer, random layers, random layers +B2, random layers +L2, random layers +R2, random layers +permute, random, random +B2, random +L2, random +R2, random +permute, and unperturbed. Each category has two bars, with distinct colors used to differentiate between the variants: blue for embedding and 1st layer, green for random models with pre-trained embedding layer, red for random models where the embedding layer is random as well, and orange for unperturbed trained models. The approximate values for the bars are as follows: embedding has an accuracy of around 80, 1st layer around 82, and unperturbed has an accuracy of around 92. The green and red bars have values ranging from approximately 79 to 82, while the random bars have values ranging from approximately 72 to 74. Notably, the bars are not sorted in any specific order, and the unperturbed bar is visually emphasized with an orange color.
